a.entradas.apkallu-oannes.titulo_alterna: Oannes, the amphibious teacher from Sirius
a.entradas.apkallu-oannes.interpretacion:
Berossus, a Babylonian priest of the 3rd century BC, relates that a being with the body of a fish and human head and feet, Oannes, came out of the Persian Gulf and taught humans writing, the arts and laws. In 1966, Shklovskii and Sagan (Intelligent Life in the Universe) cautiously proposed studying this account as a possible memory of contact, without claiming that it was one. Robert Temple (The Sirius Mystery, 1976) made it a centerpiece: Oannes and the other apkallu would be amphibious beings from the Sirius system, related to the Nommo of the Dogon of Mali, who according to Griaule knew of Sirius B, a white dwarf invisible to the naked eye.

Ancient Aliens took up the idea and added other readings of the Assyrian apkallu: the cone and bucket they hold would be a technological "handbag", and their fish headdress an elongated skull.
a.entradas.apkallu-oannes.afirmaciones.0: Temple: the Dogon had knowledge of Sirius B that could only have come from visitors from that system, the same ones as Oannes.

In his 1991 fieldwork, the anthropologist Walter van Beek found no Dogon informant who knew of Sirius B or who considered Sirius a double star; moreover, astronomy did not hold a central place in their beliefs. The data Temple attributes to the Dogon had been known in the West since 1862 and may have reached them through cultural contact (an explanation proposed by Sagan, Ian Ridpath and the Pesch brothers). Furthermore, Oannes appears in a late Babylonian source and has no documented connection with Sirius.
W. van Beek, Current Anthropology 32 (1991); Carl Sagan, Broca's Brain, 1979; Jason Colavito, "Robert Temple", jasoncolavito.com
a.entradas.apkallu-oannes.afirmaciones.1: Ancient Aliens: the "handbag" of the Assyrian apkallu would be a technological device or a symbol of alien knowledge, and the "conical head" of Oannes would prove the existence of Anunnaki skulls.

Assyrian ritual texts name both objects: the bucket (banduddû) held water or oil, and the cone (mullilu), probably a pine cone or a palm spathe, was used for sprinkling as purification. The apkallu were placed at doorways as protectors. The "conical head" is the head of the fish that forms the sage's garment, and the apkallu are the Seven Sages of Ea, not Anunnaki.
F. A. M. Wiggermann, Mesopotamian Protective Spirits, 1992; Jason Colavito, review of Ancient Aliens S6E03
a.entradas.apkallu-oannes.veredicto: The apkallu are wise, protective spirits well documented in Mesopotamian rituals; their link with Sirius comes from a disputed Dogon ethnography and has no support in the cuneiform sources.
a.entradas.enuma-elish.titulo_alternativ: The celestial battle: Nibiru versus Tiamat
a.entradas.enuma-elish.interpretacion:
For Sitchin, the Babylonian Epic of Creation is not a theogony but an encoded scientific cosmogony. Each god would be a celestial body: Apsu the Sun, Mummu Mercury, Tiamat a watery planet between Mars and Jupiter, and Marduk the invading planet Nibiru. Marduk's "winds" would be its satellites. In the battle, one of them split Tiamat: one half, pushed into another orbit, became the Earth, and the remains of the "skull" and the "tail" formed the asteroid belt (the text's "hammered bracelet") and the comets. Kingu, Tiamat's general, would be the Moon.

Alford also read the poem in astronomical terms, but in his later phase (When the Gods Came Down, 2000) he interpreted it as the memory of a planet that exploded, not as the arrival of Nibiru.
a.entradas.enuma-elish.afirmaciones.0.af: Sitchin: Tiamat is a planet that was destroyed and from which the Earth and the asteroid belt arose.
a.entradas.enuma-elish.afirmaciones.0.re: In the text, Tiamat is the primordial salt sea personified as a goddess, and from her body Marduk builds heaven and earth. It is a cosmogonic motif of the separation of the waters, with no Akkadian term of planetary meaning. Today the asteroid belt is considered material that never formed a planet, because of Jupiter's gravitational influence, and not debris from a collision.
a.entradas.enuma-elish.afirmaciones.0.fu: W. G. Lambert, Babylonian Creation Myths, 2013; Peter James (cited in the "Zecharia Sitchin" entry, Wikipedia)
a.entradas.enuma-elish.afirmaciones.1.re: Apsu is the underground freshwater ocean, which the poem personifies as a god. Peter James gives this reading as an example of how Sitchin distorts the meaning of Babylonian texts.
a.entradas.enuma-elish.afirmaciones.1.fu: Peter James, criticism cited in the "Zecharia Sitchin" entry, Wikipedia; W. Horowitz, Mesopotamian Cosmic Geography, 1998
a.entradas.enuma-elish.afirmaciones.2.af: Sitchin: the text describes Marduk as a planet (Nibiru).
a.entradas.enuma-elish.afirmaciones.2.re: Tablet V assigns Marduk the star Nēberu, "the Crossing", which regulates celestial movements. Langdon already interpreted it in 1923 as a point of intersection in the sky, and the astronomical texts associate it with Jupiter. The same poem (Tablet VI) describes how the Anunnaki make bricks and raise the Esagila temple and its ziggurat, a human building, not a spaceship.
a.entradas.enuma-elish.afirmaciones.2.fu: Cuneiform Digital Library Bulletin 2015:3, "The Marduk Star Nēbiru"; Heiser, sitchiniswrong.com
a.entradas.enuma-elish.veredicto: The Enuma Elish is a myth of creation and of Marduk's exaltation composed in the 2nd millennium BC; translating it into astronomical events depends on equivalences between gods and planets that do not appear in the Mesopotamian astronomical lists.
a.entradas.atrahasis.titulo_alternativo: The miners' strike and the primitive worker
a.entradas.atrahasis.interpretacion:
The poem of Atrahasis begins: "when the gods were like men", they bore the labor. The lesser gods, tired of digging the canals, rebel against Enlil; Enki then proposes creating the human being (lullû) to carry that labor, and the mother goddess shapes him from clay mixed with the flesh and blood of a slain god. Sitchin (The 12th Planet; Genesis Revisited) reads the episode literally: the Anunnaki assigned to the gold mines of southern Africa mutiny, and Enki and Ninhursag create a "primitive worker" (Adamu) by crossing their genes with those of a Homo erectus. The "clay" would be the female hominid's egg, and the "blood" and "flesh" (or "spirit") of the slain god, its DNA.

Tellinger (Slave Species of god, 2005) develops the idea of humanity as a slave species, and Ancient Aliens repeats it often (Jason Martell, M. J. Evans).
a.entradas.atrahasis.afirmaciones.0.afir: Sitchin: the text describes genetic manipulation between the Anunnaki and Homo erectus.
a.entradas.atrahasis.afirmaciones.0.repl: The poem describes a ritual and mythical act: shaping clay, mixing it with the flesh and blood of a slain god (We-ila) and letting the birth goddesses carry it for ten months. Lambert and Millard interpret it as a theological explanation of why humans have a divine "spirit" and must serve the gods. Neither the text nor its vocabulary alludes to species, hominids or hybridization.
a.entradas.atrahasis.afirmaciones.0.fuen: W. G. Lambert and A. R. Millard, Atra-ḫasīs: The Babylonian Story of the Flood, 1969
a.entradas.atrahasis.afirmaciones.1.afir: Sitchin and Ancient Aliens: the gods worked in gold mines and created humans to extract it.
a.entradas.atrahasis.afirmaciones.1.repl: In the poem, the gods' labor consists of digging the beds of the Tigris and Euphrates and maintaining the canals, that is, Mesopotamian irrigation. Gold does not appear as a motive. The explanation of gold for Nibiru's atmosphere is Sitchin's invention; Colavito observes that a spacefaring species would obtain it more easily from asteroids.
a.entradas.atrahasis.afirmaciones.1.fuen: Lambert and Millard, 1969; Jason Colavito, review of Ancient Aliens S6E03
a.entradas.atrahasis.afirmaciones.2.afir: Tellinger: the stone circles of Mpumalanga (South Africa) are cities of the mining Anunnaki more than 200,000 years old, including "Adam's Calendar".
a.entradas.atrahasis.afirmaciones.2.repl: Archaeologists identify most of these structures as stone-walled farming and herding settlements from the 16th to the 19th centuries (the so-called Bokoni), studied by Peter Delius, Tim Maggs and Alex Schoeman. The dating of 75,000 to 200,000 years does not come from any published archaeological method.
a.entradas.atrahasis.afirmaciones.2.fuen: P. Delius, T. Maggs and A. Schoeman, Forgotten World: The Stone-Walled Settlements of the Mpumalanga Escarpment, 2014
a.entradas.atrahasis.veredicto: Atrahasis is a myth about the origin of human labor and the role of humans in the service of the gods; the genetic and mining reading has no support in the text.
a.entradas.enki-ninhursag.titulo_alterna: Enki and Ninhursag, the colony's geneticists
a.entradas.enki-ninhursag.interpretacion:
Sitchin presents Enki as chief scientist and Ninhursag (also called Ninmah or Ninti) as chief medical officer of the Anunnaki. The Sumerian stories in which the two gods create beings would be the lab notebook of their experiments. In the myth of Enki and Ninmah, the two gods, drunk, create beings with defects; Sitchin interprets this as failed hybrids before they succeeded in creating the Adamu. In Enki and Ninhursag, the paradise of Dilmun and the plants Enki eats would be genetic trials. Sitchin also translates the name Ninti as "lady of the rib" and "lady of life" and connects it with Eve and Adam's rib.

Parks rewrites the same episodes as the creation of humans by a faction of the Gina'abul.
a.entradas.enki-ninhursag.afirmaciones.0: Sitchin: the defective beings of Enki and Ninmah are failed hybrids from a genetic experiment.

The myth is a contest between gods that explains the origin of people with disabilities and assigns them a place in society (singer, servant of the king). It is an etiological story, not a laboratory report. Moreover, the creation episode comes from Enki and Ninmah, a different text from Enki and Ninhursag.
Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Literature (Oxford), "Enki and Ninmah", 1.1.2; Thorkild Jacobsen, The Harps that Once…, 1987
a.entradas.enki-ninhursag.afirmaciones.1: Sitchin: the wordplay on Ninti (rib and life) proves that Genesis copies a cloning story.

The Sumerian wordplay on ti ("rib" and "to live") is real, and S. N. Kramer proposed it as a possible literary echo in Genesis, but it is a poetic device. It explains the name of a healing goddess in a myth about healing Enki's ribs and does not describe any procedure.
S. N. Kramer, History Begins at Sumer, 1956 (chapter on the "first paradise")
a.entradas.enki-ninhursag.veredicto: The myths of Enki with Ninmah and with Ninhursag are etiological and fertility stories; the laboratory reading is a modern reinterpretation.
a.entradas.lista-reyes.titulo_alternativ: The King List: the reigns of the astronaut gods
a.entradas.lista-reyes.interpretacion: The Sumerian King List states that kingship "came down from heaven" to Eridu and lists eight antediluvian kings (ten in Berossus) with reigns of tens of thousands of years: Alulim reigns 28,800 years, Enmenluana 43,200, and the total exceeds 241,000 years. Sitchin takes "came down from heaven" literally and turns these figures into a real chronology: measured in šar (3,600 years), they would correspond to orbits of Nibiru, and Berossus's 120 šar (432,000 years) would be the time the Anunnaki spent on Earth before the Flood. Ancient Aliens often cites these figures as evidence of extraterrestrial longevity.
a.entradas.lista-reyes.afirmaciones.0.af: Sitchin: reigns expressed in šar are equivalent to 3,600-year orbits of Nibiru.
a.entradas.lista-reyes.afirmaciones.0.re: The šar is simply the number 3,600 in the sexagesimal system (60 × 60), like "thousand" in the decimal system. The antediluvian figures are round multiples of 3,600 and 600 that express the mythical remoteness of a primordial age, just like the ages of the patriarchs in Genesis 5. Nothing in the list links the šar to a planet.
a.entradas.lista-reyes.afirmaciones.0.fu: Thorkild Jacobsen, The Sumerian King List, Assyriological Studies 11, Oriental Institute, 1939
a.entradas.lista-reyes.afirmaciones.1.af: Ancient Aliens: reigns of tens of thousands of years can only be explained by long-lived extraterrestrial beings.
a.entradas.lista-reyes.afirmaciones.1.re: The versions of the list do not agree with one another (WB 62 gives 456,000 years; Berossus, 432,000). It is an ideological document, composed around the time of Isin and Larsa, that legitimizes the succession of hegemonic cities. From the First Dynasty of Kish onward the reigns shrink to human figures, and some kings are attested in inscriptions.
a.entradas.lista-reyes.veredicto: The King List is a historiographical and political construction with a mythical antediluvian section; its figures follow sexagesimal numerical conventions and do not record real durations.
a.entradas.etana.interpretacion: In the myth of Etana, the king of Kish ascends to heaven on the back of an eagle to ask for the "plant of birth". As they climb, the eagle asks him to look down, and the earth looks smaller and smaller: first like a mountain surrounded by the sea, then like a garden, and finally it disappears. For the ancient astronaut movement, these descriptions would only be possible from a craft in flight: they would be testimony of a space journey or a high-altitude flight. Von Däniken, in Chariots of the Gods? (1968), attributed a similar description to the Epic of Gilgamesh, and Sitchin incorporates Etana into his account of the gods' travels in their "sky chambers".
a.entradas.etana.afirmaciones.0.afirmaci: The vision of the earth growing ever smaller shows real knowledge of how the Earth looks from space.
a.entradas.etana.afirmaciones.0.replica: What Etana sees is the Mesopotamian cosmological image: the earth as a mountainous island surrounded by the ocean. It is not the sphere seen from space. The earth shrinking as one gains altitude requires nothing more than having climbed a mountain or a ziggurat.
a.entradas.etana.afirmaciones.0.fuente_r: Jason Colavito, "Great moments in ancient astronautics: an imaginary ancient text", jasoncolavito.com; W. Horowitz, Mesopotamian Cosmic Geography, 1998
a.entradas.etana.afirmaciones.1.afirmaci: Von Däniken: the Epic of Gilgamesh describes Enkidu feeling a weight "like lead" and watching the earth shrink during a flight.
a.entradas.etana.afirmaciones.1.replica: Colavito does not find that passage in Tablet III, which Von Däniken cites, or anywhere else in the epic. He believes that Von Däniken confuses Gilgamesh with the myth of Etana and uses a loose German adaptation instead of a philological translation.
a.entradas.etana.afirmaciones.1.fuente_r: Jason Colavito, "Great moments in ancient astronautics", jasoncolavito.com
a.entradas.etana.veredicto: Etana's flight is a mythical motif of ascent to heaven, common in folklore (the eagle, the childless hero); its imagery follows Mesopotamian cosmology, not the real view from space.
